items.title: A.B. Spellman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 19, 2022
items.q: Pound, Ezra Pound who I don’t like to quote but sometimes do, once said that it was referred to a cycle.

ctx.x: That’s interesting because there was a similar thing happening when bebop and the “moldy figs” they called them that couldn’t absorb what was coming out of the instruments at that time.

A lot of these critics who were putting the new jazz of the 60s down had been the defenders of bebop. It’s an interesting thing, Pound, Ezra Pound who I don’t like to quote but sometimes do, once said that it was referred to a cycle. He said there’s a period when everything is set, all the rules are clear and there’s no dissention on it, and the art in those periods is sterile. And then there’s a revolution in the form and you get a lot of new artists, a lot of new artists who are taking an entirely different…

Years ago I went, it might have been the same jazz educators’ gathering that you were at. There was a panel about, that was entitled “Trad Jazz Is Alive and Well” and it had some record label people and some players. But on the program for the three or four days there was no trad jazz groups that performed. I started thinking about jazz in the larger sense has been elevated to a high art form and it’s in the universities and it is studied and you can get Ph.D.s in it but is New Orleans music and trad jazz and…
